cap:convert-format;in=\"media:enc=utf8;f.cap_description: Convert CSV data to a JSON array of objects with keys from the header row
cap:convert-format;in=\"media:enc=utf8;f.documentation:
## Purpose

Converts a CSV file into a JSON array of objects. Each data row becomes one JSON object; the CSV header row supplies the object keys. Use this when a downstream cap expects JSON but the data source is CSV.

## Inputs

A CSV file with a header row and one or more data rows.

## Outputs

A JSON array of objects, one per CSV row.

## Notes

- Column names from the header row become JSON keys. Sanitize column names upstream if they contain characters that are problematic as JSON keys.
- For YAML output, use [Convert CSV to YAML List of Mappings](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:convert-format;in="media:enc=utf8;fmt=csv;list;record";out="media:enc=utf8;fmt=yaml;list;record").
- For the reverse, use [Convert JSON Array of Objects to CSV](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:convert-format;in="media:enc=utf8;fmt=json;list;record";out="media:enc=utf8;fmt=csv;list;record").
cap:convert-format;in=\"media:enc=utf8;f.title: Convert CSV to JSON Array of Objects

args.arg_description: JSON array of objects to convert
args.name: input

cap:convert-format;in=\"media:enc=utf8;f.cap_description: Convert a JSON array of objects to CSV with headers derived from object keys
cap:convert-format;in=\"media:enc=utf8;f.documentation:
## Purpose

Converts a JSON array of objects into a CSV file. Object keys become column headers; each array element becomes one row. Use this when downstream processing or export requires CSV format.

## Inputs

A JSON array where each element is an object.

## Outputs

A CSV file with a header row derived from the union of all object keys.

## Notes

- Objects with missing keys produce empty cells in those columns.
- Column order follows the key order of the first object (or union order if keys differ across objects).
- For the reverse, use [Convert CSV to JSON Array of Objects](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:convert-format;in="media:enc=utf8;fmt=csv;list;record";out="media:enc=utf8;fmt=json;list;record").

outputs.name: output
outputs.output_description: CSV formatted data with header row

cap:convert-format;in=\"media:enc=utf8;f.title: Convert JSON Array of Objects to CSV

cap:convert-image;in=\"media:ext=png;ima.cap_description: Re-encode a PNG image as a JPEG
cap:convert-image;in=\"media:ext=png;ima.documentation:
## Purpose

Decodes a PNG and re-encodes it as a JPEG. Use when a smaller file is preferred and the loss of transparency and the introduction of compression artifacts are acceptable.

## Inputs

A PNG file. RGBA inputs have the alpha channel composited against white.

## Outputs

A JPEG file at quality 85 (default, adjustable via --quality). EXIF orientation from the source is applied to the pixels, so the output displays upright.

## Notes

JPEG does not support transparency. Alpha is composited on a white background. Quality is fixed at 85; if you need different quality, request a feature.

cap:disbind;in=\"media:document;ext=pdf\.cap_description: Extract plain text content from each PDF page
cap:disbind;in=\"media:document;ext=pdf\.documentation:
## Purpose

Splits a PDF into its individual pages and extracts the plain text content from each page. The output is a sequence of text items, one per page. Use this as the first step in any PDF processing pipeline — text extraction, summarization, search indexing, or embedding.

## Inputs

- A PDF file (path or stdin).
- An optional index range (default: `1-`, meaning all pages). Format: `1` (single page), `1-5` (pages 1 to 5), `3-` (page 3 to end).

## Outputs

A sequence of plain text values, one item per extracted page.

## Notes

- A page whose text extraction fails emits an empty-text item with a warning (same shape as a scanned page) — one bad page never aborts the rest of the document. Encrypted PDFs need `--password`.

- Text extraction works on digitally-created PDFs. Scanned PDFs (image-only) will produce empty or near-empty pages. Run an OCR step first for scanned documents.
- For visual rendering of pages as images (e.g. to feed into vision models), use [Render PDF Page Images](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:render-page-image;in="media:document;ext=pdf";out="media:ext=png;image").
- Page numbers in the index range are 1-based.

outputs.name: output
outputs.output_description: Plain text pages, one per page in the document; each page is persistable as a `.txt` file

cap:in=\"media:enc=utf8;ext=txt;plain-te.cap_description: Render a page-like PNG image preview of the text document
cap:in=\"media:enc=utf8;ext=txt;plain-te.documentation:
## Purpose

Renders a plain text file as a page-like PNG image — monospaced font, line-by-line layout. Useful for generating visual previews of text documents, configuration files, or output logs for display in image-aware contexts.

## Inputs

- A plain text file (path or stdin).
- Page width in pixels (default 800).
- Page height in pixels (default 1200).

## Outputs

A sequence of PNG images, one per page.

## Notes

- Long documents paginate: the text is wrapped to the page width by measured glyph advance (long lines wrap, they are never clipped) and split into as many pages as needed. Nothing is truncated.
- Invalid UTF-8 bytes render as the replacement character (U+FFFD) — the page shows exactly what was recoverable instead of the file being rejected.
- For log files specifically, use [Render Log Page Image](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:render-page-image;in="media:enc=utf8;ext=log;plain-text";out="media:ext=png;image") which may apply syntax-aware formatting.

outputs.name: output
outputs.output_description: PNG page images, one per rendered page

data-format.documentation:
## Data format (fmt)
The content/serialization format of a value's bytes, emitted as the `fmt=x` tag.
A value tagged with both a `fmt` and a structure tag (record/list) tells consumers
exactly how to parse the bytes into a structured representation. This is
independent of the `ext=x` file-type dim: `fmt` describes the structure of the
content, `ext` describes the file it came from / would be written to. JSON is the
default `fmt` for cap inter-step data exchange.

The textual formats (JSON, NDJSON, YAML, CSV, TSV, PSV, XML) are characters and
carry their encoding beside the format: JSON and NDJSON are always UTF-8
(`enc=utf8`, as RFC 8259 requires of JSON exchanged between systems); the others
name the encoding they are written in. The binary formats (CBOR, MessagePack,
Avro, Arrow, Parquet) are not characters and never carry `enc`. A serialization
is never `plain-text`: structured data is parsed, not read as prose.
data-format.name: data-format
data-format.title: Data Format

encoding.documentation:
## Encoding (enc)
The character encoding a textual value's bytes use, emitted as the `enc=x` tag.
Independent of `ext=` (file type), `fmt=` (serialization format) and
`plain-text` (text written to be read): `enc` describes how characters become
bytes, and nothing more.

Every value made of characters carries it. Any UTF-8 string is `media:enc=utf8`;
a JSON value is `media:enc=utf8;fmt=json`; source code is
`media:code;enc=utf8;…`; prose is `media:enc=utf8;plain-text`. A cap that
accepts any UTF-8 string takes `media:enc=utf8`; a cap that reads text as
language takes `media:enc=utf8;plain-text`.

Binary serializations (CBOR, MessagePack, Avro, Arrow, Parquet), numbers
(`numeric`) and booleans (`bool`) are not characters and never carry `enc`.
encoding.name: encoding
encoding.title: Encoding

values.documentation:
UTF-8: variable-width, ASCII-compatible, the universal interchange encoding and
the encoding of all textual content in the system. A value tagged `enc=utf8` is
a sequence of UTF-8-encoded characters; the tag makes no claim about structure
(`fmt`) or about whether the text is written to be read (`plain-text`).
values.name: utf8
values.title: UTF-8

file-type.documentation:
## File type
The concrete file format. Each value identifies a single, well-known format with its
file extensions and MIME type, contributed as the keyed `ext=<value>` tag. File-type
is the identity-axis of on-disk file media URNs: `media:document;ext=pdf` is a PDF file,
`media:enc=utf8;ext=txt;plain-text` a plain-text file. It is orthogonal to the `fmt=` content
axis — a `.csv` file holding CSV content is `media:enc=utf8;ext=csv;fmt=csv`.
file-type.name: file-type

list-marker.documentation:
## List marker
Presence marker indicating the value's content is an ordered sequence at its
root: a JSON array, a multi-row CSV, a YAML sequence, a list of strings.
Independent of `record-marker` — a value can be both (a list of records),
either alone, or neither.
list-marker.name: list-marker
list-marker.title: List Marker

values.documentation:
The value's content is an ordered sequence. Consumers can expect to iterate
elements in order.
values.name: list
values.title: List

medium.documentation:
## Medium
Medium tags declare the primary human-perceivable nature of a value: an image, audio,
a video, a document. Medium is what a person experiences when consuming the value, and
every file format of that medium conforms to the bare medium type — `media:ext=png;image`
is a `media:image`. There are exactly these four, and a value is at most one of them.

A medium is not a kind of data. Text (`enc=`), data formats (`fmt=`), numbers and
booleans carry no medium, and neither do files that hold something other than a
medium (an archive, a font, a model, a 3D mesh: the `file-kind` dim). A live feed or
a frame taken from a stream has its medium too, because it is still something to see
or hear.
medium.name: medium
medium.title: Medium

values.documentation:
The value is a visual artifact intended to be seen: a photo, screenshot, rendered
diagram, or icon. Caps that consume images (vision models, image describers) match
on this tag rather than on a specific format like PNG or JPEG.
values.name: image
values.title: Image

values.documentation:
The value is an audio recording or stream intended to be heard. Caps for transcription,
speech recognition, and audio analysis match on this tag.
values.name: audio
values.title: Audio

values.documentation:
The value is a video — a time-sequenced visual stream, typically with synchronised
audio. Caps for video processing, frame extraction, and video transcription match on
this tag.
values.name: video
values.title: Video

values.documentation:
The value is a document — laid-out pages, sheets or slides in a binary container (pdf,
docx, epub, xlsx, pptx). Caps that take pages out of a document, or put them together,
match on this tag rather than on a specific format. Writing kept as text (Markdown, RTF,
HTML) is a text file and does not carry it.
values.name: document
values.title: Document

number-kind.documentation:
## Number kind
Refines a number with its number-system domain. A number without a number-kind
tag is any number. Adding a kind narrows what arithmetic and comparison operations
are well-defined on the value, and what a reader parses: an `integer` is read as a
whole number, never as a floating-point one. A true/false value is not a number;
it is the `boolean` dim.
number-kind.name: number-kind
number-kind.title: Number Kind

values.documentation:
A whole number, positive, negative, or zero. No fractional part. Suitable for counts,
indices, ranks, and any quantity that cannot meaningfully take a decimal value.
values.name: integer
values.title: Integer

values.documentation:
A real-valued number with possible fractional part. Encoded as floating-point in
practice. Suitable for measurements, probabilities, ratios, and any continuous
quantity.
values.name: real
values.title: Real

values.documentation:
A complex number with real and imaginary components. Used in scientific computing,
signal processing, and any context requiring two-dimensional numeric representation.
values.name: complex
values.title: Complex

numeric.documentation:
## Numeric
The value is a number: something to add, compare and order. A number is its own
kind of value, never also text (`enc=`) or a data format (`fmt=`), so it reaches
only caps that take numbers; turning it into text, or text into a number, is a
cap of its own.

On the wire a number is carried as its decimal text (`42`, `-3.5`, `1e-6`), which
every runtime writes and parses. The `number-kind` dim says which numbers
are allowed; an integer-valued argument (a count, a size, a seed) is always
`integer`.
numeric.name: numeric
numeric.title: Numeric

values.documentation: The value is a number, carried as its decimal text.
values.name: numeric
values.title: Numeric

plain-text.documentation:
## Plain text
The value is text written to be read: prose, a page of a document, what OCR read
off an image, a model's description or answer. Caps that read text as language
(summarizing, classifying, embedding, prompting a model) take
`media:enc=utf8;plain-text`; anything that is plain text matches them, whatever
else it says about itself (a `.txt` file, a document page, digitized text).

Plain text always names its encoding (`enc=`), so a cap that receives it knows
how to decode it, and it is never a serialization format (`fmt=`). Source code,
markup, configuration and serialized data carry `enc=` without `plain-text`; a
cap that takes any UTF-8 string takes `media:enc=utf8` and receives those as well.
What a format holds that is meant to be read reaches the language caps through a
cap that extracts it for that format — a PDF's pages, an image's description —
written by the cartridge that works with the format.

The file types that are plain text are the prose formats: `.txt`, Markdown,
reStructuredText, AsciiDoc, Org-mode and log files.
plain-text.name: plain-text
plain-text.title: Plain Text

values.documentation: The value is text written to be read.
values.name: plain-text
values.title: Plain Text

record-marker.documentation:
## Record marker
Presence marker indicating the value's content is a key-value mapping at its
root: a JSON object, a CSV row with named columns, a TOML table, an INI file.
Independent of `list-marker` — a value can be both (a list of records),
either alone, or neither.
record-marker.name: record-marker
record-marker.title: Record Marker

values.documentation:
The value's content is a key-value mapping. Consumers can expect to address
fields by name.
values.name: record
values.title: Record

role.documentation:
## Role
Semantic-role markers distinguish how a value is used in a flow from how it is
stored. A textual file might be `code` (source code), `log` (log records), or
`page` (a single document page). Role is attached during cap declaration to make
routing decisions explicit.
role.name: role
role.title: Role

values.documentation:
The value is source code. Caps that operate on code (formatters, linters, parsers,
LSP-style analysers) match on this tag rather than on a specific language.
values.name: code
values.title: Source Code

values.documentation: The value represents a single page extracted from a multi-page document.
values.name: page
values.title: Document Page

values.documentation:
The value is the key half of a key-value pair. Used by caps that produce or
consume dict-like structures one entry at a time.
values.name: key
values.title: Key

values.documentation: The value is a separator string (delimiter, line ending, field boundary).
values.name: separator
values.title: Separator

values.documentation:
The value is a JSON Schema document — a JSON object whose contents declare the
shape of other JSON values.
values.name: json-schema
values.title: JSON Schema

security.documentation:
## Security
Security tags annotate values with handling requirements. Values tagged `secret`
are treated as confidential — log redaction, masked display, and secure-channel
transport apply automatically.
security.name: security
security.title: Security

values.documentation:
Sensitive credential or key material. Must not appear in logs or display surfaces
in cleartext. Transmitted only over secure channels.
values.name: secret
values.title: Secret

media:background-color;enc=utf8.documentation:
## Purpose
The matte color that transparent regions composite onto when converting into a format with no alpha channel (e.g. any source with transparency into JPEG).

## When to use
Set on convert-image caps that output JPEG when the source may carry transparency and white (the default) is not the intended backdrop.

## Notes
Strict format: `#RRGGBB` hex (the leading `#` is optional). Anything else is a hard error naming the expected format.
media:background-color;enc=utf8.title: Background Color (UTF-8)

media:document.description: A document, regardless of file format. The bare `media:document` URN matches any document (pdf, docx, epub, etc.); format-specific variants like `media:document;ext=pdf` refine it.
media:document.documentation:
## Purpose
The umbrella media URN for documents: laid-out pages, sheets or slides kept in a binary container. The abstract [Disbind Document Into Pages](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:disbind;in=media:document;out="media:enc=utf8;ext=txt;page;plain-text") cap takes this type, and every per-format document URN (`media:document;ext=pdf`, `media:document;ext=docx`, `media:document;ext=epub`, ...) conforms to it.

## When to use
Use `media:document` for a cap that accepts any document without committing to a format, and for an abstract cap whose specializations are all document caps. A cap that reads one format only names that format.

## Notes
Format-specific variants are produced by the `_document-file.toml` template (one entry per file-type × medium=document). Writing kept as text — Markdown, reStructuredText, RTF, HTML — is a text file (`media:enc=utf8;ext=md;plain-text`), not this medium.
media:document.title: Document

media:enc=utf8.description: Any UTF-8 string (media:enc=utf8): prose, code, markup or a textual serialization alike
media:enc=utf8.title: UTF-8

media:enc=utf8;ext=txt;page;plain-text.description: A single page of finalised plain text extracted from a multi-page document. Concrete text terminal — directly persistable as a `.txt` file.
media:enc=utf8;ext=txt;page;plain-text.documentation:
## Purpose

A per-page text payload produced by document-disbinding caps (PDF disbind,
EPUB disbind, etc.). One stream item per page; each item is the full plain
text of that page.

## When to use

`media:enc=utf8;ext=txt;page;plain-text` is the output of `cap:disbind-pdf` and
analogous disbind caps. The composite URN carries:

- `role = page` — the per-page sequence marker (so consumers know each item
  is one page rather than the entire document concatenated);
- `plain-text` — the finalised-text marker that opts into `cap:save-as-txt`'s
  persistence path;
- `file-type = txt` — binds the URN to the `.txt` extension and `text/plain`
  MIME at the registry.

## Notes

The text content is unstructured natural-language text as the disbinder
extracted it. Order is preserved across the stream (page 1, page 2, …).
Each page is its own scalar; consumers that need the whole document as one
blob should aggregate explicitly.
media:enc=utf8;ext=txt;page;plain-text.title: Document Page, UTF-8, Plain Text, Plain Text

media:enc=utf8;ext=txt;plain-text.description: Finalised plain text suitable for writing to a `.txt` file. The narrow concrete terminal type for generated or digitized text that is destined for disk persistence.
media:enc=utf8;ext=txt;plain-text.documentation:
## Purpose

Marks a text payload as **finished plain text intended for persistence**. It is
strictly more specific than `media:enc=utf8` (the generic UTF-8 text type) and is the
canonical input/output pair for the `save-as-txt` cap.

The `plain-text` marker exists to keep the planner's path-discovery from treating
every `media:enc=utf8` value as a candidate for `.txt` persistence. Without it, any
text-producing cap (PDF page extractor, JSON adapter, prompt loader) would
appear as a feeder for `save-as-txt`, polluting the recommended-paths surface with
nonsensical chains. The `plain-text` marker forces caps that genuinely produce
user-facing prose (LLM text-generation, OCR's digitized text, etc.) to opt in
explicitly, leaving intermediate text values out of the persistence path.

## When to use

- As `out` on caps that produce user-facing prose ready for disk: LLM
  text-generation caps, document-summarisation caps, code-generation caps.
- As `in` on caps that persist or display finalised text: `save-as-txt` is the
  canonical example.

## When NOT to use

- For intermediate text values that downstream caps will consume (raw page
  text from a PDF, JSON-as-text waiting for parsing, prompt strings). Those stay
  on `media:enc=utf8`.
- For structured text that carries its own format identity (Markdown, JSON, CSV,
  XML). Those use their own concrete file-type markers.

## Notes

- The `file-type = "txt"` narrowing binds this URN to the `.txt` extension and
  `text/plain` MIME type at the registry level — the writer needs no special
  handling beyond the standard extension lookup.
- The payload is UTF-8 text. No structure, no schema, no metadata side-channel.
  Token counts, finish reasons, and the like belong on the streaming-record type
  `media:enc=utf8;fmt=ndjson;llm-text-stream`; this type is the post-streaming, ready-to-save
  artefact.
media:enc=utf8;ext=txt;plain-text.title: UTF-8, Plain Text, Plain Text

media:enc=utf8;file-path.documentation:
## Purpose
Carries a single file system path as a plain-text string, used to identify the location of an input or output file on disk.

## When to use
Use this type when a machine needs to read from or write to a specific file, rather than receiving content inline. Prefer inline content media types when the file is small and the path adds unnecessary indirection.

## Notes
The path must not contain null bytes. Relative or absolute paths are both valid; the interpretation is determined by the machine's runtime context. A cap that takes several files declares its input as a sequence and receives one path per item.
media:enc=utf8;file-path.title: File Path (UTF-8)

media:enc=utf8;index-range.documentation:
## Purpose
Specifies a numeric range of indices in the format `N` (single index) or `N-M` (inclusive range from N to M), used to select a subset of items from an ordered collection.

## When to use
Use this type to select pages, lines, chunks, or records by position. Supply `5` to select index 5 only, or `2-7` to select indices 2 through 7 inclusive.

## Notes
Pattern: `^\d+(-\d*)?$`. An open-ended range (e.g., `5-`) means "from index 5 to the end"; the machine must define this behavior. See [Outline Max Depth](https://capdag.com/browse/media:integer;numeric;outline-max-depth) for depth-based selection.
media:enc=utf8;index-range.title: Index Range (UTF-8)

media:enc=utf8;pdf-password;secret.description: Password for opening an encrypted PDF document.
media:enc=utf8;pdf-password;secret.documentation:
## Purpose
Carries the password of an encrypted PDF between caps. Passed to the PDF engine for the call's duration only — never stored.

## When to use
Use this media type for any cap argument that opens PDFs (render-page-image, disbind, disbind-to-pdf, bind). Without it, an encrypted PDF fails hard with an error naming the `--password` flag; with a wrong password, the error says so explicitly.

## Notes
- The `secret` tag instructs UIs and logs to mask the value.
- An empty string is treated as "no password".
media:enc=utf8;pdf-password;secret.title: PDF Password (Secret, UTF-8)

media:integer;jpeg-quality;numeric.documentation:
## Purpose
Controls the JPEG encoder's quality/size trade-off when producing JPEG output.

## When to use
Set on convert-image caps that output JPEG. Higher values preserve more detail at larger file sizes; 85 (the cap default) is a good archival-preview balance.

## Notes
Valid range: 1-100.
media:integer;jpeg-quality;numeric.title: JPEG Quality (Numeric, Integer)

media:integer;numeric.description: Numeric primitive (integer or real) optionally as a list
media:integer;numeric.title: Integer, Numeric

media:integer;numeric;page-image-height.documentation:
## Purpose
Specifies the pixel height to use when rendering a document page as an image. Controls the vertical resolution of the rasterized output.

## When to use
Set this parameter alongside [Page Image Width](https://capdag.com/browse/media:integer;numeric;page-image-width) when you need to control the full resolution of rendered pages. Increasing height improves vertical detail for tall or portrait-oriented documents.

## Notes
Valid range: 50–4000 pixels. Aspect ratio handling is machine-specific. For most document types, setting only width and allowing the machine to infer height is simpler and avoids distortion.
media:integer;numeric;page-image-height.title: Page Image Height (Numeric, Integer)

media:integer;numeric;page-image-width.documentation:
## Purpose
Specifies the pixel width to use when rendering a document page as an image. Controls the horizontal resolution of the rasterized output.

## When to use
Set this parameter on page-rendering or PDF-to-image machines when the default resolution is too low for OCR or visual analysis, or too high for bandwidth-constrained pipelines.

## Notes
Valid range: 50–4000 pixels. Pair with [Page Image Height](https://capdag.com/browse/media:integer;numeric;page-image-height) to set both dimensions. Aspect ratio enforcement is machine-specific; some machines may adjust one dimension to preserve proportions.
media:integer;numeric;page-image-width.title: Page Image Width (Numeric, Integer)
